projection.rationale: Revenue declines sequentially from Q4FY26 peak due to lower zinc prices and normalised volumes (~260kt refined), but remains well above Q1FY26. OPM at 53% reflects cost guidance of $975-1000/ton and removal of Q4's INR 600cr gross-up, partially offset by hedging drag.

Modest sequential volume improvement to ~270kt and steady LME. OPM ticks up to 54% as fertiliser plant and hot acid leaching ramp up, boosting by-product credits and lowering net cost toward $975/ton. PAT reflects stable other income and tax rate.

Volume reaches ~280kt as Debari smelter contributes initial tonnes. OPM expands to 55% on higher grade (7.3-7.4%) and RE share reaching 30%, reducing power cost. Revenue growth muted YoY as Q3FY26 had an exceptionally high 55.1% OPM base.

Full-year exit rate of ~290kt refined metal; revenue capped by normalised zinc prices (~$2900). OPM sustained at 55% as cost stays within guided band. PAT growth QoQ from operating leverage, but YoY decline due to absence of Q4FY26's INR 600cr gross-up and favourable one-offs.

bull_bear.body: Net Cash position INR 5,594 cr; Gross Cash ~INR 14,000 cr. Dividend: First interim dividend for FY27 declared at INR 11/share (~INR 4,300 cr); FY26 final dividend was INR 10/share. Policy: Minimum 30% payout of PAT maintained alongside growth funding. Brand/Strategic Services Fee to Vedanta: ~INR 1,300 cr for FY26.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Commodity Price Volatility (Zinc/Silver); Geopolitical impact on energy/input costs (diesel, propane); Mining grade variability; Regulatory changes in critical mineral auctions; Execution risk on 1MTPA consolidated smelter.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and celebratory regarding record operational/financial metrics; Pragmatic on cost guidance (factoring uncertainties); Strategic on consolidation (1MTPA smelter) to optimize capex; Disciplined on hedging (10-20% band) and capital allocation (balancing dividends and growth).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Accounting gross-up: New ancillary agreements for waste-to-wealth create ~INR 600-1,500 cr symmetrical entries in 'Other Operating Income' and 'Other Expenses', inflating top-line and opex without net P&L impact. Silver strategy: Production volume is inversely managed against zinc prices (maximize zinc when LME >$3,000, shift to lead/silver if zinc falls), making silver output a flexible margin lever rather than fixed volume. Consolidation logic: Shifting from multi-site smelters to a single 1MTPA hub in Rajasthan reduces logistics costs of moving concentrate.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Clear dividend policy: minimum 30% of PAT or 5% of opening net worth, whichever is higher; delivered ~5.6% dividend yield.
- Focus on maximizing total shareholder returns; FY25 TSR of ~68% (₹198.60 per share), 13x NIFTY 50 returns.
- Maintains AAA credit rating and industry-leading balance sheet; FY25 ROCE of 58% and ROE of 73%.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- **Funding math disclosed explicitly:** run-rate PAT of ₹12,000–13,000 crore/year → ~₹60,000–65,000
  crore over 5 years, against a ~₹40,000–45,000 crore capex need. Management's framing: **capex is
  fully funded from internal accruals "without hurting any shareholder gains,"** with debt used only
  opportunistically to match cash-flow timing — reads as an implicit **no-dilution signal** (no rights
  issue/QIP flagged) even though a shareholder directly asked whether a rights issue or QIP would be
  used.
- **Dividend track record cited:** FY26 final dividend ₹10/share; **first FY27 interim dividend already
  declared at ₹11/share** (paid Apr/May 2026) — consistent with the "minimum 30% payout" policy noted
  in the Q4FY26 concall note.
- **Total shareholder return since the 2002 disinvestment:** ~₹787/share including ~₹285.55/share of
  cumulative dividends — cited by management as …
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation & dividend signals (AGM 2026)

bull_bear.body:
- Chairperson's speech was aspirational and identity-shifting ("the best chapters of Hindustan Zinc
  are not behind us"), leaning into the metals-to-energy-transition repositioning and citing
  India's projected 2031 critical-minerals demand-supply gap (domestic production meeting only ~10%
  of national demand) as the strategic opportunity.
  CEO Arun Misra's tone was confident/comprehensive — his single consolidated Q&A response covered
  nearly every shareholder question in one pass (a shareholder jokingly noted this left nothing
  for others to ask).
- **Clean audit opinion** — no qualification, modified opinion, or adverse remarks; notice/auditor's
  report were taken as read given no exceptions.
- **Governance recognition:** first Indian company in ICMM; #1 global ranking in metals & mining on
  S&P Global Corporate Sustainability Assessment for the 3rd consecutive year; top 1% …

business.body: Zinc: Record production (315 KT mined Q4, 282 KT refined Q4); Cost $903/ton (Q4), $959/ton (FY26). Silver: 176 tons (Q4), 627 tons (FY26), contributing 45% to profitability. Lead: Strategic sale of 12,000 tons concentrate in Q4 (Rev ~INR 500 cr, EBITDA ~INR 330 cr).
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Rising input costs and supply deficits in green energy metals | Tata Power | beneficiary | Med | HZL's increased sulfuric acid output (by-product of zinc) supports domestic fertilizer and industrial demand, indirectly stabilizing supply chains for power/agri sectors; HZL's own renewable push (35% by FY27) aligns with green power procurers. |
| Silver supply deficit impacting solar PV manufacturing | Waaree Energies | beneficiary | Low | HZL's focus on maximizing silver recovery (target 830 tons by 2029) adds marginal domestic supply to the tight global silver market used in solar panels. |
| High zinc prices increasing galvanization costs | JSW Steel | loser | Med | As a major zinc consumer for galvanizing, sustained high zinc prices ($3,200+/ton) pressured by HZL's production discipline (prioritizing zinc over silver when prices are high) may keep input costs elevated. |
business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers

business.body:
- World's largest integrated zinc producer with 77% domestic primary zinc market share in India.
- Only integrated and listed silver producer in India, ranked among the top 5 silver-producing mines globally.
- Ranked 1st in Metals & Mining sector in S&P Global CSA 2024 for the second consecutive year.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

latest_quarter.body: Revenue: INR 13,544 cr (Q4, +49% YoY), INR 40,844 cr (FY26); EBITDA: INR 7,747 cr (Q4, 57% margin), INR 22,162 cr (FY26); PAT: INR 5,033 cr (Q4, +68% YoY), INR 13,832 cr (FY26); Order Book: N/A (Commodity producer); Net Debt: Net Cash of INR 5,594 cr (vs Net Debt INR 1,169 cr in FY25). One-offs/Accounting: INR 600 cr annualized 'other operating income' and matching 'other expenses' from new ancillary waste-to-wealth agreements (grossing up P&L); Hedging delta drag of INR 1,100 cr in Q4 and INR 1,500 cr for FY26 vs spot prices.
latest_quarter.title: Financial scorecard

latest_quarter.body: Q4 Cash Cost $903/ton (lowest since underground transition, -9% YoY) driven by higher grades (7.9%), 64% domestic coal mix, and by-product credits. FY27 cost guided at $975-$1,000/ton factoring grade normalization (~7.3-7.4%) and geopolitical input risks. Renewable energy target 30-35% in FY27 (from 18% in FY26) to drive long-term cost down ($1/ton saving per 2% RE increase).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

outlook.body: Revenue Growth: Volume-led (Mined metal 1.15M tons, Refined 1.1M tons in FY27); Margin: Supported by cost guidance of $975-$1,000/ton; Order Inflow: N/A; Capex/Commissioning: $500-600M for FY27 growth projects; Debari 250KTPA smelter mobilized; Fertilizer plant commissioning early 2QFY27; Hot Acid Leaching commissioning 2QFY27.

outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body: Consolidating planned expansions into a single 1MTPA smelter in Rajasthan (vs multiple smaller units) to reduce capex intensity; Secured 3 critical mineral blocks (Potash, Tungsten, Rare Earths); Tailings reprocessing at Rampura Agucha; Targeting 830 tons silver production by 2029 via LGLC circuit and smelter expansion.
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
Chairperson Priya Agarwal Hebbar reframed the company's ambition from "world's leading integrated
zinc producer" to a **"future-ready energy transition company"** — building strength across multiple
metals rather than remaining zinc-only. The core commitments:
- **2X volume plan:** double total metal production from **1.1 million tonnes to 2 million tonnes over
  the next 5 years**, via brownfield expansion + de-bottlenecking (no new-geography greenfield
  mentioned).
- **Capex envelope:** **₹40,000–50,000 crore** multi-year programme (CEO later reiterated as "40 to
  45,000 crore" in the Q&A). **Phase 1 of ₹17,000 crore already Board-approved in FY26**, covering a
  **250,000 TPA integrated zinc smelter at Debari** and **India's first zinc tailings-reprocessing
  plant**. Balance ₹23,000–33,000 crore of the programme is not yet phase-approved — watch for
  slippage/approval cadence.

deepdive.thesis: HZL delivered record Q4FY26 financials driven by a historic low cash cost of $903/ton and 45% profit contribution from silver, validating its cost-curve advantage. Management signaled a strategic pivot to a consolidated 1MTPA smelter in Rajasthan to maximize scale, while maintaining a disciplined 10-20% hedging policy and committing to a >30% dividend payout despite aggressive growth capex.

verdicts.item: Board approved first interim dividend of INR11 per share (~INR4,300 crores) for FY27.
verdicts.note: Shareholder Manoj Sharma states 'is saal bhi April aur May mein ₹11 ka dividend diya hai', confirming the first interim dividend of INR11 per share was paid.

verdicts.item: FY27 mined metal production guidance of 1,150 KTPA, plus or minus 10 KT
Silver production guidance for FY26 is 680 tons plus/minus 10 tons, and the company expects to be close to this guidance.
A fatality occurred at Rajpura Dariba mine; corrective and preventive measures are being implemented with urgency and learnings disseminated.
verdicts.note: Corrective measures and safety protocols are being implemented, including collision avoidance system at SK mine.

verdicts.item: The company will continue to operate in zinc-plus-lead mode (not lead-only mode) given strong zinc prices, maximizing both zinc and silver output.
verdicts.note: CEO explained they tilt production towards more zinc when zinc prices are up, but operate in zinc-plus-lead mode, not lead-only.

verdicts.item: Silver production in Q4FY26 is expected to be better than Q3FY26 (158 tons) due to favorable conditions and completed shutdowns.
verdicts.note: Q4FY26 silver production was 176 tons, which is better than Q3FY26's 158 tons. Transcript: 'Our quarterly silver production stood at 176 tons, up 11.0% sequentially.'

verdicts.item: Strategic hedging policy targets 10-20% of annual zinc and silver volumes to lock in margins when market prices exceed business plan/consensus.
verdicts.note: Management stated they are comfortable at 10% hedging, within the 10-20% target range.

verdicts.item: Renewable energy share in power mix was 20% in Q3FY26, expected to exit FY26 at 25%, reach 35-40% in FY27, and 70% thereafter.
verdicts.note: FY26 exit RE was 18%, missing 25% target; FY27 guidance is 30-35%, below 35-40%.

verdicts.item: Maintenance capex for FY26 is expected to be around $400 million for the full year, with ~$90-100 million in Q4.
verdicts.note: Total capex INR3,600 crores minus growth INR2,000 crores implies maintenance ~INR1,600 crores (~$190 million), below $400 million. [±10% rule]

verdicts.item: Total growth capex for FY26 is expected to be around $300 million, with $180 million spent by December and an incremental ~$120 million in Q4.
verdicts.note: Growth capex for FY26 was INR2,000 crores (~$240 million), below the expected $300 million. [±10% rule]
